runner: scripted, outside the repository, on a native-Linux git-archive export of the commit: apply edits (each find verified to occur exactly once) -> tsc -b (TypeScript) or node --check (.mjs) -> node --test --test-reporter=tap <kill set> -> killed when the kill set exits non-zero (a failed test, a failed hook or a cancelled test) -> restore original bytes -> SHA-256 compare -> rebuild after a TypeScript mutation; then the whole export diffed against a fresh git archive of the commit
history: A first campaign on 122e6e1 (M1-M32) was stopped after M13 when the first adversarial review's fixes changed mutated code. A run on e2e0304 was stopped at M21 when the second review's fixes did. A complete run on 87c1736 (M1-M41) found M23 SURVIVED -- dropping the execution-outcome store from a restore went unnoticed because the committed claim also prevents a duplicate execution -- and counted M31 as survived only because its runner read the TAP fail count, while M31 makes the integrity suite's before() hook fail (tests cancelled, exit code 1); M37's find string was stale. The drill was strengthened (the restored outcome record must name the pre-backup grant, 6cc0529), the runner switched to the kill set's exit code and M37's find was corrected. The authoritative run recorded here is the complete run on 6cc0529.
